recent_posts.title: Closing the Loop: Building Shapes with a Planar Graph — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of creating closed shapes from disconnected agent paths using computational geometry. The process involves agents that draw paths using Perlin noise for smooth movement, detecting intersections to avoid overlapping edges, and then building a planar graph with half-edges to trace complete loops. The technique transforms scattered line segments into fillable shapes by following left-most turns at junctions until returning to the starting point.

recent_posts.title: A Message Drifts — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: A detailed technical breakdown of creating generative art that combines algorithmic symbol placement, procedural sentence generation, and glitch aesthetics. The system uses a 16-symbol alphabet positioned on Perlin noise flow fields, generates grammatically correct sentences from templates and word lists, implements custom handwriting rendering, and applies various glitch effects like repetition and stretching. The piece explores how randomness can create the appearance of meaningful communication through careful system design and collision detection.

recent_posts.title: Chaos in the medium: watercolour plotting — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: This post explores the author's experience of combining watercolour painting with code using an AxiDraw plotter. It discusses the set up process, testing outcomes, different types of brushes used, achieving smooth lines, creating typographic pieces, layering techniques, and future exploration ideas.

recent_posts.title: Meaningful Nonsense: How I generate sentences — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses a system in JavaScript that generates sentences of "meaningful nonsense". The author shares examples of sentence structures, curated word lists, and rules for fitting words together. They explain how nouns and verbs are altered for different contexts and discuss the use of semantic similarity for labeling diagrams. The post also mentions the creation of "truths" and the generation of content for handwritten artworks. The author emphasizes the meaning-nonsense continuum and invites readers to contemplate the potential meaning behind the generated sentences.

recent_posts.title: A strange kind of physical reality — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: A long-form generative art project inspired by quantum theory will be released on fxhash in partnership with FAB DAO on 11th Jan 2024.

recent_posts.title: Meaningless — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: Meaningless is an ArtBlocks project that explores the concept of intrinsic meaninglessness and the power of randomness and algorithms. The algorithm uses geometry and structural rules to create varied forms, and the resulting images can be interpreted differently by each viewer.

recent_posts.title: Early Computer Art in the 50’s & 60’s — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: Explore the development of computer art in the 50's and 60's, including early examples of electronic art, notable computer artists, and early exhibitions of computer-generated art.

recent_posts.title: Midjourney takes on Sol LeWitt’s Wall Drawings — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: The post explores the implementation of Sol LeWitt's 'Wall Drawings' using the AI image generation tool Midjourney. It compares Midjourney's interpretation of the instructions to ChatGPT and provides examples of different prompts given to Midjourney. The post highlights Midjourney's ability to create aesthetically pleasing outputs and its potential as an inspiration tool for generative art.

recent_posts.title: AI Generations: ChatGPT-3 vs ChatGPT-4 on Sol LeWitt’s Wall Drawings — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: This post compares the outputs of ChatGPT-3 and ChatGPT-4 in implementing Sol LeWitt's Wall Drawings. GPT-4 shows improvements in interpreting the instructions more accurately, producing more sensible code, and creating aesthetically pleasing results. The post discusses the differences between GPT-3 and GPT-4 in various wall drawings and highlights the potential for using AI as a collaborator in generative art.

recent_posts.title: Forecast — Amy Goodchild
recent_posts.summary: Forecast is a long-form generative art project featuring abstract paintings created using algorithms. The project explores the use of algorithms to produce aesthetically and emotionally impactful images. The elements in Forecast include background daubs, swoops, paint, triangles, constellations, and overlay shapes.
